criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC01; scope 1, 1A, 6; DM "Shared contracts", "Design decisions"
criteria.sufficiency: E1 shows a run requested through the supported path outliving its initiating client under host ownership; S1 confirms the registry and its lifecycle are created and owned by the existing Harness host, not a new daemon or parallel control plane. Together they establish host ownership behaviourally and structurally.

AC02 is the client-detachment claim; E1 disconnects the initiating client after launch and shows the Harness-owned run continues and is not lost while the host is alive - the direct falsification test.
AC03 is the reconnect-and-inspect claim; E1 has a later client resolve and inspect the same active or terminal run by its stable Harness run identity.

AC04 enumerates the run-record contents; E2 asserts the canonical run record exposes each listed field (slot, execution attempt, role, executor, invocation mode, workspace, permission profile, lifecycle, timestamps, process/provider identity) in a stable observable form, and does not invent unavailable metadata.

AC05 requires the methodology attempt and the execution attempt to be distinct and observable; E3 replaces a worker, creating a new execution attempt for the slot without a new methodology attempt, and shows both identities separately observable.

AC06 is the single-active-execution claim; E4 issues two concurrent/repeated start requests for one active slot and shows at most one child/provider execution, with a concurrency-safe check and allocation.

AC07 constrains the duplicate-request response; E4's decision rule requires the duplicate to return/identify the existing run or fail with an explicit conflict, never a second worker - the `200`-or-conflict choice itself is Design Map freedom.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC08; scope 5, "Failure and recovery semantics"; DM "Shared contracts"
criteria.sufficiency: AC08 is the replacement-ordering precondition; E5 shows a replacement cannot be allocated while the prior canonical execution for the slot is still active.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC09; scope 5; DM "Shared contracts", invariant 4
criteria.sufficiency: AC09 requires the replacement record to preserve prior identity, new identity, reason, and executor change; E5 allocates a replacement and asserts each of those is recorded, including the fallback-executor case.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC10; scope 6, 1A; DM "Shared contracts", "Design decisions"
criteria.sufficiency: E6 shows the canonical `tools/workflow.ts` path requesting/attaching to a host-owned run and failing explicitly when no host is reachable; S3 confirms it no longer directly owns detached child processes; S1 confirms the run mechanism is the existing host, not a parallel methodology daemon.
AC11 is the terminal-completion-binding claim; E7 shows the runner refusing to record a phase complete unless the canonical run for the matching phase/attempt is terminally `completed`.

E8 shows structured events distinguishing allocated, started, activity, completed, failed, cancelled, and replaced; S4 confirms those events reuse the existing Harness structured-event protocol rather than a second event system.

E9 shows execution text/logs inspectable and tied to the run but not a frozen methodology artifact, downstream context, or completion signal; S4 confirms the diagnostic-log handling structurally keeps that separation.

AC14 enumerates the routine operations a standard worker must perform without per-command prompts; E10 exercises repository reads/writes, local computation including shell child processes, tests/checks, and role-permitted Git within the allowed workspace with no human prompt.

E10 shows an evaluator run declaring an additional private evaluator workspace; S2 confirms that profile differs from the standard one only by adding that declared workspace and grants no arbitrary unrestricted host access.

criteria.frozenAuthority: spike.md AC16; scope 10; DM "Design decisions", invariant 5
criteria.sufficiency: S2 confirms the default local backend uses an explicitly named workspace-bounded profile and not an unrestricted-bypass mode, with any bootstrap exception explicit in the Design Map/execution record; E10 shows routine work completing without that mode.
E2 asserts the permission-profile identity is a field on the run record; E10 shows it recorded for a concrete run; S2 confirms the recorded value names the applied bounded profile.

AC18 enumerates the cheap run metrics; E11 asserts the run records elapsed time, executor, execution attempt/replacement count, and terminal disposition from directly observable facts, omitting rather than estimating unavailable provider usage.

E7 shows a directly launched process with no canonical run identity failing to satisfy the runner's completion requirement despite plausible artifacts; S3 confirms a direct external process has no usable run identity for the slot.

E1/E4/E5/E7/E8/E9 are the enumerated behaviours (client detachment, duplicate-launch prevention, replacement ordering, terminal-completion binding, event visibility, diagnostic-log/noncanonical separation); E12 shows them driven through an in-memory backend seam with no live paid provider call; P1 confirms the visible suite runs green.

AC21 is a set of command exit codes plus continued green pre-existing suites at the evaluated commit; P1 records `npm test`, typecheck, lint, `format:check`, `git diff --check`, and the session/backend suites.
